saying: Commenters accept synthetic data only as a supplement — for rare events, adversarial and stress testing, controlled perturbations, and privacy-limited coverage — and not for establishing performance rates, subgroup claims, or benefit-risk conclusions. Most ask FDA to guard against correlated blind spots through generator lineage disclosure and separation, independent or multiple generators, real-world holdouts, and separate real/synthetic reporting.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on whether synthetic-to-real adequacy can be demonstrated: some would allow pooled or supplemental use if generators are independently validated against real distributions and transportability or distributional shift is analyzed, while others say no validated method exists for showing distributional adequacy and FDA should assume none does.

sides.summary: Synthetic data can supplement or be pooled if generators are independently validated against real distributions and shift/transportability is documented.
No validated method exists to show a synthetic population is distributionally adequate to a real one; FDA should presume none and bar synthetic data from performance-rate and subgroup claims.
